entities.summary:
The German invasion of the Netherlands in 1940 was a pivotal event in European history, marking the beginning of a brutal occupation that would last for five long years. On May 14, 1940, German forces led by General Heinrich von Vietinghoff-Scheel launched a surprise attack on the Netherlands, quickly overwhelming the Dutch army and forcing Queen Wilhelmina to flee the country. The invasion was part of the larger Battle of the Netherlands, a pivotal moment in World War II that would set the stage for the Nazi occupation of France and the Low Countries.

The occupation that followed was marked by brutal repression, forced labor, and mass deportation of Jews and other minority groups to concentration camps. The Dutch people were forced to live under a strict curfew, and any form of resistance was met with severe punishment. The occupation lasted until May 5, 1945, when Allied forces finally liberated the country.

The legacy of the German invasion of the Netherlands is one of sorrow and loss, but also of resilience and courage. The Dutch people's determination to resist and ultimately defeat the Nazi occupation served as a beacon of hope for the rest of Europe, and their bravery and sacrifice will never be forgotten.

As one historian noted, "The occupation of the Netherlands was a dark chapter in European history, but it also serves as a reminder of the enduring spirit of the Dutch people."
